purpose: Gate tier for hamzated/weak/doubled-root decisions. norm() over-recalls weak roots; certification needs norm_strict + QAC, never the lenient key.

rules.when: the root would be inferred from norm() alone for a weak/hamza stem (إِلَيْنَا→ل ي ن; إيمان/أيمان; قُرْءَانًا+نا)
hamza-seat distinction is meaning-bearing (أ/إ/ؤ/ئ/ء) and could collapse under norm()
hollow/defective/assimilated root whose radical is hidden/alternating (قَالَ ق-و-ل; دَعَا د-ع-و; يَجِدُ و-ج-د)
rules.note: recover the radical from QAC/the family before authoring

rules.when: QAC root+POS confirm the weak root AND a single Qamus sense applies AND no homograph
QAC root/POS contradicts the proposed reading

voice_signature_gate.purpose: An unvocalized (harakah-free) skeleton never licenses a voice reading, and a voice is never defaulted to active. Voice is committed ONLY when a candidate surface byte-matches the melody-templated active OR passive form the paradigm generator (verb-measures.json, read-only, via tools/fusha_paradigm_generate.py:generate_verb) actually produced for the same lemma/measure/slot; a match to both, a match to neither, or the absence of harakat all abstain. Operationalizes sarf@2.1 sarf-passive-vocalism-voice-commit (SKILL.md) without releasing or promoting it.

hollow_pattern_vowels.purpose: A hollow (أجوف) root's C2 (middle) pattern vowel must be on record from the recovered muḍāriʿ family (procedures/weak-root.md step 3) before its abstention reason may cite the sharper hollow_root_c2_hidden gap; an unrecorded root still abstains (RM-40 never templates a weak radical) but must never be reported as a generic weak-root abstention when the true defect is a specifically HIDDEN, never-recovered C2 vowel.

lafif_compositions.purpose: A لفيف root carries two weak radicals recovered by two ordered operations (procedures/weak-root.md's لفيف rule: 'recover both, never read one as a long vowel'). مفروق (C1+C3 weak, e.g. وَفَىٰ ← و ف ي) and مقرون (C2+C3 weak, e.g. طَوَىٰ ← ط و ي) each require BOTH operations attested IN ORDER; a surface consistent with only one operation, or with the operations out of order, fails composition and must abstain rather than certify a half-recovered root.
